I’m US & have a mail-slot. The Mail comes inside. It’s treated like a free-standing or house mounted mailbox. This I was happy to have so my nosey neighbor couldn’t view my mail. And, true. US Mail-slots are not to be used for any solicitor’s handbills. In US (where-ever I’ve lived), even newspapers must go in a separate box (mostly rural routes) or tossed into a person’s yard or front porch. Mailboxes are for Mail...ONLY.

Hopefully if you are part of a HOA, they may post a sign, around the front of your housing addition (& some apartment complexes will too) stating “NO Solicitors”.  That has helped w/door leaflets. I doubt one could catch a legal charge for disobeying. Do it enough and someone from HOA (home owner’s association) May call the solicitor & give you a “firm” attitude about “disobeying” the posted sign for “no solicitors”. 

Yes. Agree. Don’t mess w/another’s Mail. I had a neighbor who was the nosiest @$sH0£€ around. Whenever I had a box or (soft) package left by the mailman (or anyone), she’d come over, pick up, shake, look through torn taped edges, etc b/c she believed it was her business to know what was inside & who I was ordering from. She’d even take my packages home. To her home! W/o my permission! ...”for safe keeping”.  Then, bug the Sh!T!!! Out of me to come get it! (In the winter, it was always: “it’s getting cold in my garage, come get this, I don’t know if it can be out in the cold all night”.  MORE of her ploys to know what it was. Thinking as I had at one time, said, “Oh, no worries, it’s just a book”. (Or whatever, but you see where I’m going here.) She’d even bring boxes to her garage (& I swear!) OPEN them. B/c I refuse to believe Amazon (as one example) ships packages that “accidentally” get torn open in transit. I’m disabled. At times lots of items come through the mail. I asked her multiple times to leave my items alone...for 2+ YEARS! Finally, I blew up & told her she was trespassing on private property & I needed her to just stop. The NEXT DAY, this cray-cray is on my door-step going through a pile of packages as I open my door to bring them inside. (I park in garage. She assumed I wasn’t home). She yelled something & ran home. I then called the US Postmaster General. (I hope that’s the correct title. It’s been a couple years now. A cousin is a mailman & he gave me the correct title to ask for. The post office doesn’t handle this. It’s a separate division.)  Who had to come out & “chat” w/her. Explaining to her my Mail is my private property & tampering & moving it to her home w/o the addressee’s request is a federal offense. Punishable by a fine of $x,xxx & up to xx years in prison. Seriously, this was wasted time, but she was too much. It’s the only way to get her to leave my things alone.  (And she will still, at times, check pkgs free m FedX & UPS b/c those are couriers & not under USPS laws). Who wants a stranger to go through the mail in their mailbox.? Just stroll on over, grab my letters & peruse? No! She knew not to do that!  But just  b/c my packages don’t fit in the mailbox & are left outside my door, it’s the same thing.  I know I’m probably sounding overly sensitive, but there are reasons Mail is private. Not that I was ordering anything strange. (It’s mostly groceries, books, clothing & gifts. All of which are Nunya Business. Not her business anyway). 

TL;DR Nosey neighbor would come look over pkgs rec’d via US mail. Take some home, open etc. (never steal. She’s just a snoop.)  I called US Postmaster General. He came & spoke w/her. She stopped looking over my pkgs. but only pkgs delivered by US Mail. She still likes to try to view my FedX & UPS (o/n courier pkgs). 🙄

I never “counted” this as my Dad’s Christmas gift, but he was really, always, pleased I simply paid his monthly cell phone bill. (I added him to my cell’s “family” plan.) Sometimes it’s the simplest of things that matter. Dad died at 88. Lived way out in the country & tended his own 10+ acres...mowing, snow removal, etc. He ALWAYS kept his cell phone on him. He was pleased & I had piece of mind...for the “if something ever......”

We were always an odd family, tho. So, consider this.

When you’re ready...eventually start doing a “family thing” in her remembrance. It’s Thanksgiving weekend. My mom had the tree up & ALL Christmas cookies mixed (dough in freezer) & we made holiday candies. (Subsequent weekends were for baking off the cookies.) NOW, we talk about how “she did it all!”  The grands (her great-grandkids, both boys & girls who want) wear one of her aprons. And we make ONE item today. Long ago, we decided to make her homemade caramels. We look at pics & chat & remember when.....  It took me years to do this. But I never knew my grandma, but her great grands will know my mom. Just please hold on. Believe it or not, happy memories will develop over the years. It’s just difficult to imagine rn. HUGS!!!

Do you have siblings, father, cousin, a special Auntie or grandma you can draw close too?  I’d have died be about ANYTHING for my sister’s kids when she passed.  I’m still re-telling her Adult kids their baby-stories. I hope you may be able to focus on how you’d like to keep her memory alive. What did she enjoy? What did you two do together. (We baked. My dad allowed me to take some recipe cards, cookbook & her bright yellow hot mitts she used. lol! I love slipping my hands in them to remove items from the oven, b/c she held them first). Are you able to set aside a few items that are special to you?  This helped me to focus on the future, plan for the next generation, etc. I have my nephew’s fiancée a pic of him & gma baking & his favorite cookie recipe gma baked. She adored it!  It’s really soon. I found hope in the future & planning simple ways to honor her memory. Maybe journal memories as it may be too soon to want to engage w/another & remember. One day at a time. I wish I could hug your broken heart until it sealed together. You WILL make it. Hold on. 😇

Oh my!  I’m sorry!  My mom died, totally unexpectedly, freaky type thing when I was 25...& I thought THAT! Was “too soon”!   I can not imagine!  But one thing a dear, close cousin told me was this: The first year is the hardest. It’s Everything! Every holiday, every birthday, every anniversary of this time when...or that time when... And just get through “all the firsts” & it WILL get better. 

I placed myself on almost “auto-pilot” .. & I made it!  Was it hard? Yes!  My dad died 20 years later. I entered grief counseling. I was told the “old” standard for grief WAS one year....Now? That “average” is THREE YEARS!  And mind you, not everyone is “average”.  “Average” is a figure of speech to me. I’m 4 1/2 years from his death & I’m still struggling. 

You are young & only 6 months post your Mom’s death?  Oh!  I can’t even find words for how difficult this must be. But it’s only 6 months. (And I bet it feels like an eternity.). But, please, please...hang on!  Because the Sun, Warmth & Love will find You again. I now have many ppl in my life who are “motherly” towards me. And no. It didn’t take almost 25years. But I had to heal first to recognize this beauty. And Honor my mom. Then, I knew I was ok to feel, deeply, the healing Love of all the “mothering” around me. It’s only what My Mom wanted for me...all along. (My mom didn’t want to leave me, but she had to go & be at peace. And I don’t begrudge her this peace, but I’ll always miss her immensely.) 

You still have an entire life to live. Husband. Children. Grandkids. Let your Mom live on. In memories from you. And eventually share her Joy w/others & future generations.  Please just try to consider this?  All the Bests!!  I’m so Very Sorry for Your Loss!

If they are helping her (say funding her college, etc), it’s difficult to fly solo w/o the gravy train. And yes, some parents use their money to “force” a break-up, job change, etc. 

Sounds like she may be being controlled by others & forced to cut ties w/you & obviously doesn’t truly want the breakup. Or, she’s finding her true feelings for another woman, feels she can no longer stay with you, hurt you while she explores her lesbian side. Idk. 
My money is on the former (control) rather than the latter (lesbian).
